title: Review of c01's Marangoni-droplets finding: on seed 4 no arm self-propels and all end as static lattices (replicated), but alpha=+20 gives fewer persistent splits than alpha=0 (Weak)
summary: Seed 4 labkit reruns of world.py with WORLD_P alpha = +20, 0, -20 and ampf = 0.05 (my reading of 'force scale 0.05'; the packs do not record the arm parameters). Final bodies 22 / 14 / 6 and splits 33 / 12 / 5, so the direction of the alpha effect on division activity holds, and -20 suppresses division (0 persistent). But persistent splits are 5 at +20 against 8 at alpha=0 (generation 1 vs 2): at +20 the founders are shredded by strong early flow into ragged, speckled fragments (rerun_a20/seed4/sheet.png t=800-4400), so most splits are fragmentation that does not persist for K=2000, not cleaner division. No arm self-propels (max 3.1 / 1.6 / 0.8 body lengths, speeds <= 0.006) and every arm ends as a static droplet lattice, as the finding says.

observations.I: rerun_a0/seed4/sheet.png and rerun_a20/seed4/sheet.png t=10000-20000: discrete static droplets (14 and 22), no motion beyond 3.1 body lengths

seeds_run.result: partial: no propulsion and static end state replicate; persistent splits +20: 5 < alpha=0: 8 (finding: 14 > 10/12); -20: 0 (finding: 6)

verdicts.limitation: The arm parameters are not recorded in the packs; I assumed WORLD_P {alpha, ampf: 0.05}. If 'force scale' is another parameter my rerun is not the claimed world. One seed; the persistent-split ranking may be seed-dependent, since labkit counts fragmentation at +20 that does not persist.
